texts.preamble: Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No.: 2/2022 Fir no.: 417/21 Ps : Pul Prahladpur U/s 279,338 Ipc & 3/181,5/180 M V Act Cnr No.: Dlse01-0004902022 Suraj Pal S/o Sh. Kishan Pal R/o B-168, Gali No.9, Shiv Durga Vihar, Lakkarpur, Faridabad, Haryana. .....Petitioner Versus Ali S/o Sh. Rashid Ali R/o M-25, Gali No.5, Saurabh Vihar, Jaitpur, New Delhi. ............Driver/Respondent no. 1 Raj Kumar S/o Sh. Jagan Nath R/o H.No. 77, Nehru Marketing Badarpur, New Delhi. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 The New India Assurance Company Ltd. Legal Building, 1st floor, Core-3, Scope Minar, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi-110092. .......Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Mact No: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 1 Of 23 Bk Date of accident : 24.08.2021 Date of filing of Dar : 20.01.2022 Date of Decision : 29.02.2024 Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (DAR), filed by the police on 20.01.2022, in terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act and the same is treated as a claim petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 24.08.2021, on receiving information regarding accident vide DD no. 57A, police official reached at the spot but neither offending vehicle nor injured was Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143397911/ 1 met. After receiving DD no. 65A, the police reached AIIMS Trauma center where injured Suraj Pal was met. The injured informed that on 24.08.2021, he was going to his house after closing his shop on a bicycle towards Lakkarpur via M.B. Road and Pul Prahladpur. HR-38S-3077(hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and hit his cycle, due to which he fell down and received grievous injuries. The driver of the offending vehicle came to the victim and advised him to take immediate treatment, while assuring to return and left. The police was informed about the accident by someone and upon arrival, they took the victim to the hospital for treatment. 3. The injured filed a complaint through his nephew on 06.09.2021, upon which an FIR no. 417/21 u/s 279/338 of IPC & 3/181, 5/180 MV Act was registered at PS Pul Prahladpur and MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 2 Of 23 BK the matter was investigated. It is pursuant to the investigation that a charge sheet u/s 279/338 &3/181, 5/180 MV Act was filed before Ld. MM and a DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Pursuant to notice issued to the respondents, respondents (including driver, owner of the offending vehicle and Insurance company with which such vehicle was insured) appeared and filed written statement. As per reply filed by Respondent no.1/driver and Respondent no.2/owner, allegations of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle have been denied. It is pleaded that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by another vehicle. Involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident is altogether denied. Even Respondent no3/insurance company has denied its liability on the ground that there is a delay of 14 days from the date of accident,in registration of the FIR. It is pleaded that apart from the injured himself, there is no independent eye witness to prove the accident or involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident. It is pleaded that the accident, if any, occurred due to the negligence of the injured/petitioner. It is further doubtful that the injured sustained injuries of grievous nature as the Medical treatment record does not referred to exact nature of the injury sustained by him, in detailed. 5. Insurance company/Respondent no.3 has also raised statutory defence by pleading that the driver of the offending vehicle did not hold a valid driving licence for the category of the vehicle which was being driven by him at the time of accident. It is thus, pleaded that a breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy would not entail a liability on the insurance MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 3 Of 23 BK company. 6. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 16.09.2022. 1. 7. Thereafter, evidence was led through local commissioner, by the petitioner by examining claimant Sh. Suraj Pal as PW-1. PW-1 led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and relied upon copy of his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1(OSR), copy of PAN Card as Ex.PW-1/2(OSR), proof of shop as Ex.PW-1/3, Copy of Medical treatment record as Ex.PW-1/4(Mark-X), copy of discharge note as Ex.PW-1/5(OSR), copy of DAR as Ex.PW-1/6 and original medical bills as Ex.PW-1/7(colly). PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.1 and Respondent no. 2 and also by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.3. Thereafter PE was closed. 8. Respondent no.1 and 2 examined Sh. Raj Kumar by of his affidavit as Ex.R-2W/A. He relied upon copy of Insurance Policy, certificate of fitness, permit and driving licence of R- 1/driver as ExR-2W/1(colly) and Mark R3W1(colly). He was cross- Respondent no.3/insurance company examined Mr. Rahul Verma as R-3W-1 by way of affidavit as Ex.R-3W-1/1 and relied upon letter of authority as Ex.R-3W-1/2, insurance policy as Ex.R-3W-1/3 and Notice as Ex.R-3W-1/4. 12 In the present case, petitioner/injured has specifically deposed that on 24.08.2021 at about 9 PM, he was riding bicycle and going to his home from Tigri, New Delhi. When he reached MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 5 Of 23 BK in front of petrol pump, Lal Kuan, Pul Prahladpur, a truck Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143397911/ 3 (Hywa) bearing no. HR 38S 3077 came at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit him from behind. Petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries in his rib, spine and all over body. He was taken to JPN Apex Trauma Center, AIIMS, New Delhi and remained hospitalized till June, 2022. Further, he was running his shop at Tigri and was earning Rs.18,000/- p.m. and due to such accident, he is unable to run his shop till date. He deposed that he had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards his treatment/special diet, conveyance and other expenses. 13. On being cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.1 and 2, PW1 denied to have been walking alongwith his cycle on the left side. He denied that the injuries sustained by him were not a result of any rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. He denied being drunk/intoxicated at the time of the accident or that he was himself negligent in having lost control over his cycle. He testified that he received injury on his left ribs after being hit on his spinal cord by the offending vehicle and stated that he had not undergone any surgery on his spinal cord after the accident. Further, in his cross-examination by Respondent no.3, PW-1 admitted that apart from the documents filed on record, no other documents had been brought to show that the injured was running a shop or a stall at Tigri at the time of accident, PW-1 stated that he did not file any ITR to maintain any profit or loss account but denied the suggestion that he was not running any shop at Tigri near mother dairy or that he was not earning MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 6 Of 23 BK Rs.18,000/- p.m. He admitted that he had not filed any medical certificate to show that he had been advised by the doctor to be on bed rest or abstain from working. He denied having not spent Rs.2 lacs on his medical treatment and admitted to be suffering from diabetes since prior to the accident. He admitted that he had not placed any prescription of treatment between 31.12.2021 to 14.03.2023. He denied document Ex.PW-1/3(proof of shop/stall hawker Joint Action Committee, Vending certificate and application made to SDM dtd 30.05.2018) and Ex.PW- 1/7(Original medical bills) to be forged and fabricated. The nature of injury as disclosed in the Medical treatment record, observes L2 burst fracture with retrolisthesis of CT spine. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 7 Of 23 BK charge sheet against Respondent no.1 under Section 279/338 of IPC & 3/181, 5/180 MV Act which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner/ claimant/applicant and against the respondents. Accordingly, Issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the petitioner.
texts.arguments: It is further submitted that the relevant insurance policy was effective and valid w.e.f. 20.12.2021 to 27.06.2022 and thus no liability can be fastened upon the insurance company. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 20. The following observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs. Tata Aig General Insurance Company Limited And Others (2018) 7 SCC 558 is relevant to the present facts and quoted as under: Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143397911/ 5 ''...15. We may fruitfully note that the three-Judge Bench adverted to situations where the driver does not have a licence and the same has been allowed to be driven by the owner of the vehicle by such person, the insurer would be entitled to succeed in defence and avoid liability, but the position would be different where the disputed question of fact arises as to whether the driver had a valid licence and where the owner of the vehicle committed a breach of the terms of the contract of insurance as also the provisions of the Act by consciously allowing any person to drive a vehicle who did not have a valid driving licence." 22 . As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 10 Of 23 BK The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 23. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143397911/ 6 (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a MACT NO: 2/2022 Suraj Pal v. Ali P.No. 11 Of 23 BK consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 23.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143397911/ 9 fit and accordingly granted in the present case. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 32. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". The expression used in guideline No. (iv) issued by this Court is that in the case of literate persons also the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i), whereas in the guideline Nos. Suraj Pal (Dar) vs Ali (417/21, Ppp) on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143397911/ 11 (i), (ii), (iii) and (v), the expression used is that the Tribunal should.
